children: Solar stocks fell sharply on Thursday, led by First Solar's
10.3% plunge to a new 52-week low, as high borrowing costs add pressure to an industry that depends heavily on project financing.
Losses among solar stocks were broad, including Enphase Energy
down 0.7%, SolarEdge Technologies
down 4.3%, Shoals Technologies
down 3.4%, Nextpower
down 2.2%, Fluence Energy
down 1.5%, Clearway Energy
down 3.1%, Sunrun
down 6.8%, Canadian Solar
down 3.4%, Enlight Renewable Energy
down 5%, Eos Energy Enterprises
down 9.3%.
U.S. long-dated Treasury yields have climbed to multiyear highs in recent days, extending a global selloff, as the Iran war raised energy prices and as investors worry about government spending.
The yield on 30-year Treasury bonds climbed to 5.48%, highest since 2004, on Thursday, while the benchmark U.S. 10-year yield hit 5.2% after breaching 5% only last week.
Recent business activity data pointing to strong U.S. economic growth but with rising inflation pressures has raised the chances the Federal Reserve will continue to raise interest rates.
In the solar industry, projects often require substantial upfront capital before generating revenue or reducing energy costs, making financing conditions particularly important.

Also, Trump administration officials indicated that an offer to advance stalled wind and solar projects as part of negotiations with Democrats on legislation to speed energy permits could be withdrawn if a deal is not reached soon, Bloomberg reported.

Reports say it is looking increasingly unlikely that the Senate would hold a vote on permitting reform before heading home for midterm campaigns, particularly as the House is not expected to convene again until after the November elections.

title: First Solar leads big solar sector drop as high borrowing costs threaten project financing
